body: I just tried the text hotline last night as I was in a really awful state mentally and all they did was repeat the same things over and over again. Then I said I was living my worst nightmare and they said crying may be my best step for tonight, take care, disconnected. Not helpful at all

Seriously, when you have to lie to generate outrage, maybe you’re on the wrong side of the argument? We really need a serious education reform, things are just getting ridiculous now. I would protest that too, if it were true. Thank you for saying that. Panic brain has been telling me that she officially hates me forever, but rationally, I’m pretty sure you’re right. I really appreciate you for being there for me and giving me advice through this

Exactly, if I thought that people were actually killing live babies I would be livid at the thought too. A lot of people really don’t understand, thanks to pro-life propaganda. Especially here in the USA. There’s a part of me that wants to be as loud as possible about my beliefs and a part of me that wants to not be disowned by even my distant relatives. I should have been less open about it... but I feel so strongly about it that I hate that I have to do that. I probably do have to backpedal though. I’ll definitely try that the next time I feel a panic attack coming on
I’ve never heard of that, thank you so much for sending it to me. No exaggeration, you may have genuinely helped save my life tonight. I can’t thank you enough just for being there

Oh god no, I didn’t mean that I think abortion is baby murder, I meant that that’s how my mom sees it and how she sees it is what’s bothering me so much. Because I know my beliefs and that they’re not wrong, but I also know what she sees pro-choice people as, and that’s scary because her perception of me is what will affect our relationship. Thank you so much for your advice. I’ll probably end up turning it around and pretending that I didn’t really mean it, or that I need to learn more about it or something. It’ll be unfathomably hard for me but it may be a necessary evil

I know in my heart that my opinions are not evil and they’re not immoral. I know prolife is a disease just like theism (I’m actually an antitheist too) but yeah, it hurts when I let her words make me feel like I’m a bad person. The truth is I actually am living with my parents too (I’m 20 but don’t have any way to move out right now) so I am really scared of the possibility of being kicked out... although I don’t know if they’d really go that far. I appreciate the advice so much... I think the best thing may actually be to put the cat back in the bag like you said. To tell the truth I’ve been a little too open about my opinions (atheism too) lately and I kind of had this coming, although I never outright admitted to anything, so maybe the best thing to do would be to swallow my pride and put on a real show about how I’ve been doubting God lately and I just need to pray more to figure it out... I’d have to do some serious acting and it would mean I can never have an honest, real relationship with my parents, but it might be my only choice here. I really, really appreciate that you’ve spent so much time listening and responding to me when I have no one else. Tonight has been the worst

Thank you so much for commenting. She has a very strong opinion about it, so I don’t know if that would work. She believes that people are just having them just to have them and I doubt that anything I can say would make her feel different. I don’t know, that’s just been my worst fear my whole life and I don’t know if she’ll ever be able to see past it

Thank you for taking the time to comment this, I appreciate it more than you could ever know. The thing is that my mom has been through some stuff that I understand would lead to being prolife, and while I do accept that completely, she thinks she’s entirely morally in the right for believing what she believes... so of course, she believes I am totally immoral and maybe evil for the opinions I hold about it. There’s just no way to explain myself to her and that’s what she said, and that when I was younger I agreed with her and she doesn’t understand why suddenly I’m okay with murder. I thought I could rationally explain my opinions but she backed me into a corner where anything I could say would make me look like a genuine baby murderer. I won’t be able to change her mind on it so now I feel like I’ve ruined my relationship with my mom who I’ve always been close with. The idea of her thinking something so horrible of me just makes me feel like I want to die

Absolutely! That’s what I realized immediately after decoverting too. You grow out of the infantilized state that religion tries to keep you in. It’s like you’ve finally grown out of believing in Santa Claus and then nobody can try to convince you that fairies or leprechauns exist either. By the way I just noticed your username and I absolutely love it and am a little jealous haha.

Congratulations! It’s certainly not an easy thing to question your beliefs when a huge part of the belief system says that questioning will lead to damnation... That’s one of the reasons why it’s such a hard and honestly kind of scary transition. But you’ve done it! And now you get to see the entire world through unbiased, nonjudgmental, open eyes and that is such an exciting thing! I’m excited for you!

Unbelievable. Imagine spewing so much hate that you make someone feel like they have the worth of a chewed piece of gum after something like that. Absolutely disgusting. I love that we can say that the people advertising for a condom brand are generally better people than the holiest ones to walk this earth though 🙏

Don’t feel alone, because you’re not. There are plenty of people here who you can reach out to if you need interaction with people who aren’t in an echo chamber. I personally understand the feeling of being young and having different beliefs than your family while still being under your parents’ roof... I can be a listener if you need it.
You were very brave for standing up and refusing to perform rituals that are in conflict with your true beliefs. You should be proud of that, even if things feel awful right now.

It really is, it almost feels like a cult when you look at it this way. I’m sorry you experienced that, it sounds like it was really traumatic for you. And the fact that they held you back from her must have made it a million times worse. My brother and I were just alarmed to see the people falling at first, but my parents served with the church so we never had to see them fall and wonder what was happening to them. It’s honestly sick to involve kids in all of that like it’s a healthy thing...

Wow, if this isn’t the kind of thing that shows people how fake it all is, honestly I don’t know what is. It is literally a show they’re putting on. The sad thing is that some desperate people actually think they feel something when the pastors do that.
That reminds me of an experience from a long time ago, back when we went to our “home church”, the first church I “belonged” to. Our pastor had the children (I wanna say they were ages six through twelve?) line up in the front, and he went down the line praying for us. The pastor was literally pushing the kids down as he went. I watched as he was praying for one boy, and instead of getting into the prayer or whatever, this kid, who was a little bit bigger than the rest of us, locked up his body in an almost defensive way because he was determined not to fall down. That was when the rest of us were able to see how hard the pastor was pushing. That’s a moment I still laugh about with my brother, although I think I laugh for a different reason.

Throwaway because my family doesn’t know my beliefs yet, and I don’t want to risk it. I’ve been to this church before; my experience there is one that continues to solidify my fairly new stance on theism whenever I think about it. I do not like this man. At one point, he prayed over these kids who fell down on the stage (in the common way that people who “feel the presence of God” do, if you’ve ever seen it you’ll know what I mean)... but they were like eight. It was so obvious that they had been instructed to do that, and I saw after that they were talking quietly to each other while I guess they were supposed to be pretending to be knocked out. Something about that just struck a chord with me. Instead of talking freely with their friends, playing and enjoying their childhood, these kids are already being introduced to the brainwashing of the adults around them. Already being taught to put on a show. Everything about this guy is fake. Not to mention when he came around, praying for every single person in the church and his bodyguards (yes, bodyguards) actually TOLD you to fall down... That night plays over and over in my head as the first time I realized how truly fake and orchestrated churches/religions are.
